title: Caramelised Kouign-Amann Pastries
summary: Flaky, buttery pastries folded into flower shapes with layers of sugar that bake into a crunchy caramel crust.

ingredients.item: strong white bread flour, plus a little for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt
unsalted butter, melted, for the tins

ingredients.note: 50 g for the tins, 150 g for the folds and rolling, 60 g for shaping

steps.title: Tins
steps.text: brush 6 alternate holes in each tin with melted butter and sprinkle each with about 1 tsp of sugar (50 g in all).

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: knead the flour, yeast, salt, melted butter and water on low until it comes together, then on medium 8-10 min until smooth and it stretches thin without tearing. Cover and leave in a warm place 1 h until puffy but not quite doubled.

steps.title: Butter
steps.text: fold baking paper into an 18 cm square packet, put the cold butter inside in slices and beat and roll it into an even, pliable 18 cm square. Chill. Press the air out of the dough, flatten to a disc, wrap and freeze 30 min until very cold.

steps.title: Laminate
steps.text: roll the dough to a 30 cm square, set the butter on it like a diamond and fold the corners over to enclose it. Roll to a 60 x 25 cm strip and fold in 3 like a letter. Turn 90°, roll and fold again, then wrap and chill 30 min. Give it a third roll and fold. Cold butter in thin layers turns to steam in the oven and pushes the layers apart.

steps.title: Sugar fold
steps.text: roll a fourth time to 60 x 25 cm, sprinkle the middle third with 40 g sugar, fold one end over, sprinkle with 40 g more and fold the last third over. Chill 30 min; if the butter softens at any stage, chill 20 min.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: scatter 30 g sugar on the worktop, roll the dough to 34 x 45 cm and scatter 40 g more on top. Trim the edges and cut 12 squares of about 11 cm. Sprinkle each with 1 tsp sugar, fold the 4 corners into the centre, press down and set in the prepared holes.

steps.title: Prove
steps.text: cover loosely and leave 45-60 min in a warm (not hot) place until puffed and the layers start to open. Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan) with the foil-lined tray on the shelf below.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: bake one tin at a time, 15 min, then lower to 175 °C (155 °C fan) and bake 15-20 min more until deep golden with dark caramel at the edges; the centre should read 93 °C. Turn the oven back up for the second tin. Cool 5 min, ease out with the palette knife and cool caramel side up on the rack. Spacing them in alternate holes lets hot air reach every side so they caramelise evenly.

tips: A common mistake is letting the butter warm up; if it feels greasy or soft, chill the dough for 20 min.
Prove somewhere warm but not hot, or the butter melts out before baking.
Unmould while still warm, as the caramel hardens and sticks once cold.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best on the day. Keep in an airtight box for up to 2 days and warm at 180 °C (160 °C fan) for 4 min.
